title: Hidden comment markers on the forge and the tracker

kind.description: active for a value in force; tombstone for a value withdrawn, which the chapter keeps listed so its identity is never reused. It is not part of a value's identity, so withdrawing a value changes only this field.

name.description: The record kind's name in the records registry, which an enveloped record's kind field carries; null for a marker that is not a record.

part.description: marker for a hidden marker of a record kind, not-record for a marker that is not a record, envelope-field for a field of the record envelope.

marker.description: One hidden marker, as its comment opens after `<!-- `; what follows it is its kind's own. A kind with several markers has one value for each. For an envelope field, the field's name.

fieldType.description: For an envelope field, the JSON type of its value; null for every other value.

fieldRequired.description: For an envelope field, whether every record carries it; null for every other value.

medium.description: forge or tracker; null for a marker that is not a record.

version.description: The schema version Jig's writers write now, which its envelope's v carries; 0 for a kind whose records carry no version; null for a marker that is not a record.

key.description: For a kind whose records carry the envelope, the whole shape of its key as a regular expression; null otherwise.

writtenBy.description: Jig, or for a kind Jig only reads, the tool or the person that writes it; null for a marker that is not a record.

meaning.description: What the record is for to a reader that meets it, and what that reader does with it; for a marker that is not a record, why it is not one.

values.name: dispatch-rearm-request
values.meaning: Binds the rearm label to the ledger comment and generation that a person asked to restart. The newest trusted record for the label takes precedence, and a withdrawal ends the request.

values.name: drive-ledger
values.meaning: The drive's resumable state, mirrored onto the pull request at each round boundary, park and takeover: who drives it, its round, what is parked and how the drive stands, so a drive started in another clone or on another machine resumes where the last one left off. Only a driver writes it; of two ledgers the earliest trusted comment is the ledger.

values.name: summary-answer
values.meaning: The drive's answer to a review finding the reviewer could not anchor to a line of the diff. A round groups its answers in one comment, with a distinct outcome, reason and fingerprint marker for each finding. Trusted markers let a retry skip delivered answers.

values.name: summary-answer
values.meaning: The drive's answer to a review finding the reviewer could not anchor to a line of the diff. A round groups its answers in one comment, with a distinct outcome, reason and fingerprint marker for each finding. Trusted markers let a retry skip delivered answers.

values.name: thread-reply
values.meaning: A reply on a review thread. Its last-line marker says the thread was answered and is deliberately left unresolved, the reply asks a question and carries no outcome, or its outcome is provisional and a person may reverse it. A marker counts only as the reply's last line, and does not prove who wrote it.

values.name: thread-reply

values.name: deferred-section
values.meaning: The findings a pull request deferred, one entry each in its body, which are filed as tracker issues once it merges or closes. A person's text outside the markers is never touched.

values.name: deferred-section
values.meaning: The findings a pull request deferred, one entry each in its body, which are filed as tracker issues once it merges or closes. A person's text outside the markers is never touched.

values.name: drive-answer
values.meaning: A person's answer to one parked question, written by `jig send`: the re-arm reads its `answer <key>:` line from a trusted author and hands the answer to the next pass. The same record answers a need's decision, on a tracker item too, where it is how the dispatcher tells a person's answer from its own identity's other comments. Each person's latest answer counts.

values.name: ai-review-summary
values.meaning: The AI reviewer's summary comment, with the commit it reviewed and any notice that it skipped one, from which the drive learns whether the head was reviewed and what the review left open. The markers are the repository's configuration; the one listed is the default.

values.name: ai-review-round
values.meaning: The review round a reviewer's comment belongs to, and the findings the reviewer held out of its threads. The drive reports explicitly non-blocking entries for inspection and counts blocking entries as summary findings to answer.

values.name: ai-review-round
values.meaning: The review round a reviewer's comment belongs to, and the findings the reviewer held out of its threads. The drive reports explicitly non-blocking entries for inspection and counts blocking entries as summary findings to answer.

values.name: coderabbit-comment
values.meaning: A review bot's follow-up on an answered thread that carries no new finding (a confirmation after a push, or an acknowledgement of a reply), which the drive lets pass without an answer.

values.name: coderabbit-comment
values.meaning: A review bot's follow-up on an answered thread that carries no new finding (a confirmation after a push, or an acknowledgement of a reply), which the drive lets pass without an answer.

values.name: coderabbit-review-body
values.meaning: A finding the reviewer put only in the body of its review, never in a thread, marked with its id, which the drive reads as a summary finding to answer.

values.name: tracker-footprint
values.meaning: An item's predicted repository paths and change areas, its source and base commit. The running pickup's newest prediction stands; otherwise the newest trusted record stands, with labels or unknown when absent.

values.name: do-item-pr-association
values.writtenBy: the session following the do-item skill
values.meaning: Binds a tracker item to the exact pull request opened for it, where no issue-link line is required, so the item's parent roll-up can tell whether that pull request merged. A link in any other comment is no evidence.

values.name: deferred-batch
values.meaning: The issue that collects one pull request's deferred findings of one type, found by its key so that each finding is appended to it rather than filed alone; of two with one key the oldest wins.

values.name: tracker-claim-marker
values.meaning: The token a claim posts on an item before it writes the item, naming the claim's attempt, its session, its branch and the claimant, so another tool sees which session holds the item, and of two hosts claiming it at once the earliest marker wins; a claim a person started ahead of the item's open blockers adds an override naming their reason, the person and each blocker's key and state, which never decides who holds the item; beside it, each attempt records once how it ended (claimed, released or unresolved), and a marker whose attempt recorded released or unresolved holds nothing.

values.name: tracker-related
values.meaning: A link from one GitHub issue to another, written as a comment before GitHub had related links: read as a link until the migration converts it to GitHub's own and marks it superseded.

values.name: tracker-related
values.meaning: A link from one GitHub issue to another, written as a comment before GitHub had related links: read as a link until the migration converts it to GitHub's own and marks it superseded.

values.name: tracker-attachment
values.meaning: A file attached to a GitHub issue, its text carried in the comment or a link to a hosted copy. A carried file whose text no longer has the size its marker records reads as changed, never as the file.

values.name: tracker-blocked
values.meaning: That an item was moved to blocked because its pull request's drive stopped, naming the pull request, the stop and the state the item left, so one stop blocks the item once and the item returns only to that state.

values.name: issue-fields-sweep
values.meaning: That the weekly sweep found an issue incomplete, naming the facets it lacks and the retired labels it carries: it moved the issue back to triage, or, where the repository keeps the sweep from moving issues, left it where it is. A run that stopped before the move finds the comment and moves the issue without posting again; where the sweep does not move issues, a later run passes over an issue that carries it.

values.name: reflection-github-store
values.meaning: The GitHub reflection store: an issue per change, and comments holding the change's events, read only from authors who can write to the repository.

values.name: reflection-github-store
values.meaning: The GitHub reflection store: an issue per change, and comments holding the change's events, read only from authors who can write to the repository.

values.name: fleet-health-suspicion
values.meaning: A suspicion the fleet-health sensor raised on an epic, of work that shows ceremony without progress: never a diagnosis, which only a person's comment on the epic makes.

values.name: epic-acceptance-verdict
values.meaning: A person's verdict on an epic, `ACCEPT`, `ACCEPT-WITH-FOLLOWUPS` or `REJECT`, on the comment's last line. The fleet-health sensor counts an epic accepted when its newest verdict from a trusted author accepts it.

values.name: epic-sweep
values.meaning: Identifies the rows in an epic closure proposal by their digest. The reply applies to that proposal.

values.name: epic-waiver
values.meaning: Records a person's acceptance of an epic closure proposal. An epic may close with this waiver when its newest trusted acceptance verdict is absent or accepting.
a waiver a person writes in a document, which the docs skill's deferral check reads
the banner the change-areas skill writes at the top of a file it generates
the banner the docs skill writes at the top of an index it generates
The record's kind, as the records registry names it. A kind the reader's registry does not hold does not read.
The version of its kind's schema the record was written in, from 1. A version newer than the one the reader's release writes does not read.
What the record is about, unique within its kind (on the forge and the tracker, within its repository), in the shape its kind declares.

Who wrote it: the forge login where the writer knows it, the host, and the boot, process id and start time of the writing process. On the forge and the tracker the host and the boot are digests, so a public comment names no machine.
When it was written, as an ISO 8601 time.
For a record rewritten in place, or a claim on one round of something, a count: one past the highest the writer had read, or the round it claims.
